title: Admission to a Level of the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan
content:
A level of the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan is open to a guest only where the guest meets its minimum
driver age and its minimum marketplace driver score on the day the trip starts, and a guest who meets neither is
quoted the levels they do qualify for rather than refused protection altogether.

A level will not cover a vehicle the marketplace values above the level's exclusion ceiling, nor a vehicle in
one of the level's excluded value classes, and where the trip is on such a vehicle the guest must elect a level
that does cover it before the trip can start.

Declining marketplace protection is open only to a guest who evidences their own motor policy carrying at least
the level's minimum third-party limit, and the guest's word that they are insured is not evidence of it.

Commercial carriage, and any trip crossing an international border, are covered only on the levels that say so,
and a trip of that kind on a level that does not cover it leaves the guest carrying the loss themselves.

A guest may choose a level only for a trip that has been confirmed and has not yet started, since a level chosen
after the vehicle has been collected would cover a risk already taken.

Additional drivers are approved up to the level's maximum, each one charged at the level's additional driver
fee, and a driver who has not been approved before the trip starts is not covered at all.

## Where the evidence must come from

**Evidence of the guest's own motor policy.** Where a guest declines marketplace protection, the insurer
standing on the election record, together with the election reference and the level recorded on it, is what the
marketplace reads before the level is taken, and the third-party limit that policy carries must be at least the
limit written for the level. What the guest says about being insured is not evidence of it; the record is.

**The state of the trip.** The trip beneath the election must stand as booked on the Keyturn Trip Booking record
correlated by the booking reference, read before the level is taken. A trip that has not been confirmed, and a
trip on which the vehicle has already been collected, do not satisfy the condition.

## Admission read as a checklist of conditions

| Condition | Read against | Satisfied when |
|---|---|---|
| Driver age and marketplace driver score | The level's minimum age in whole years and its minimum score, on the day the trip starts | Both are met |
| Vehicle value and value class | The level's exclusion ceiling and its list of excluded classes | The marketplace valuation does not exceed the ceiling and the class is not on the list |
| Own motor policy, where protection is declined | The insurer recorded on the election and the level's minimum third-party limit | The record shows a policy carrying at least that limit |
| Kind of journey | Whether the level covers commercial carriage and a trip crossing an international border | The level says so |
| State of the trip | The Keyturn Trip Booking correlated to the election | It is confirmed and has not yet started |
| Additional drivers | The level's maximum number of additional drivers | Each driver is approved before the trip starts |

## Two hypothetical admissions

A guest of 22 whole years with a marketplace driver score of 69 meets the minimum age of every level written for
21 and meets the minimum score of Keyturn Minimum Protection, whose score is 68, but not of Keyturn Standard
Protection, whose score is 70. They are quoted the levels they do qualify for.

A trip booked on a vehicle the marketplace values at 140000.00 USD stands above the exclusion ceiling of Keyturn
Standard Protection, which is 120000.00 USD, and under that of Keyturn Advantage Protection, which is
175000.00 USD. Where the guest wants the trip to start, the level elected must be one that covers the vehicle.
